Yuan.docx.old_text: RNA extraction used TRIzol; reverse transcription used PrimeScript RR047A, followed by SYBR RT-qPCR on PikoReal 96. Each target and paired β-actin reference was measured once per rat, without technical replication. Within-rat ΔCq was target minus reference Cq. Relative quantity was calculated as  and divided by the arithmetic mean quantity of the six sham rats [7]. This assumes equal, approximately 100% amplification efficiencies. Original Cq, amplification and melting exports are provided in Supplementary File 7. Target melt profiles were heterogeneous, and two wells had conflicting plate/result annotations. Efficiencies and β-actin stability were not validated; no-template/no-reverse-transcription control records were unavailable. The six supplied records per group were retained unchanged for exploratory reporting. Reagent details, primers, protocols and source-flow information are retained in Supplementary Methods.

Yuan.docx.old_text: Interpretation remains constrained by regional rather than RVLM-specific sampling, heterogeneous target melt profiles, conflicting qPCR well annotations, incomplete validation and untraceable cross-assay identities. Later restoration observations confound implant removal with age, elapsed time, recovery and repeat anesthesia/surgery. Omission of postoperative analgesia raises animal-welfare concerns and possible pain/stress confounding. Small exploratory samples and male-only inclusion limit precision and generalizability. The same-day model–sham comparison supports a regional phenotype; validated assays, anatomical localization and time-matched controls are required to investigate NOX-dependent sympathetic mediation or an implant-removal effect.

Yuan_supplementary_information.docx.old_text: Source review identified unresolved plate/result annotation differences: Nox1 model well B10-Ch5 (Cq 29.82) and Nox4 sham well D12-Ch5 (Cq 34.69) were labelled Empty/[none] in the Plate worksheet but Unknown with numeric Cq values in Cq Results. The laboratory explanation and native .ord files were unavailable. Target melt profiles were heterogeneous, with broad peaks, shoulders or additional peaks in the supplied images. Reported Tm values also varied, including Nox1 B10-Ch5 (78.59°C) and E11-Ch5 (75.76°C), and Nox4 D12-Ch5 (77.97°C) and F13-Ch5 (73.98°C). The software setting "Max # of peaks = 1" does not establish single-product amplification. Consequently, target specificity could not be confirmed. All six originally supplied records per group were retained without post hoc exclusion; transcript estimates and associated tests are exploratory and do not establish validated gene-specific quantification.
Yuan_supplementary_information.docx.new_text: Source review identified plate/result annotation differences: Nox1 model well B10-Ch5 (Cq 29.82) and Nox4 sham well D12-Ch5 (Cq 34.69) were labelled Empty/[none] in the Plate worksheet but Unknown with numeric Cq values in Cq Results. After reviewing source records, the authors confirmed that these Plate entries were annotation errors: B10-Ch5 was a Nox1 model sample and D12-Ch5 a Nox4 sham sample. Original exports and Cq values were retained unchanged. The supporting loading/laboratory record was not included in the supplied archive, and native .ord files were not supplied. Target melt profiles were heterogeneous, with broad peaks, shoulders or additional peaks in the supplied images.
